source_verification: MT Prov 14:32 reads בְּרָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶה רָשָׁע וְחֹסֶה בְמוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק. In Biblical Hebrew, חסה ("seek/take refuge") takes a protector rather than death as its shelter; with absolute Qal participle חֹסֶה, בְמוֹתוֹ functions temporally/circumstantially ("in/at his death a righteous man has a refuge"), paralleling the circumstantial sense "in his calamity" alongside instrumental "by his evil" for בְּרָעָתוֹ. The prior English "takes refuge in his death" forced "his death" as the shelter itself.
applied_changes: Updated verses[14:32] and native_verses[14:32] to "A wicked man is overthrown by his evil, while in his death a righteous man has a refuge." (keeping exact MT בְמוֹתוֹ without importing LXX or adding "even"); expanded notes[14:32] / native_notes[14:32] to explain choseh bemoto temporal syntax alongside bera'ato ("by his evil" / "in his calamity"); also logged HEB-HQ-044 in pass2_human_editor_queue.jsonl for final human editorial confirmation on this classic Wisdom crux.

source_verification: MT Neh 4:7 (וָאַעֲמִיד מִתַּחְתְּיּוֹת לַמָּקוֹם מֵאַחֲרֵי לַחוֹמָה בַּצְּחִיחִים וָאַעֲמִיד אֶת־הָעָם לְמִשְׁפָּחוֹת...) has no pronoun after the first וָאַעֲמִיד and suspends its object אֶת־הָעָם ("the people") until the resumptive verb. Inserting "them" at clause start collided with v. 6's outlying Jews. Expansion scan across all repeated 1cs wayyiqtol verses in Nehemiah (2:15, 4:7, 7:5, 13:19) confirmed 4:7 was the sole referent collision.
applied_changes: Reordered object naming in verses[4:7] and native_verses[4:7] to "So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the exposed places—I stationed them by families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows." (preserving both occurrences of וָאַעֲמִיד with unambiguous referent) and appended a brief resumptive-syntax note to 4:7.

source_verification: MT Exod 37:14 definite הַמִּסְגֶּרֶת refers back to מִסְגֶּרֶת introduced twice as "frame" in 37:12 (and rendered "frame" in parallel Exod 25:25, 25:27). applied_changes: Changed "Alongside the rim were the rings" to "Alongside the frame were the rings" in both native_verses[37:14] and merged Saints verses[38:10].

Caught identical coreference switch for בְּרִיחַ: rendered "crossbar(s)" in 26:26-29, 35:11, 36:31-33, and 40:18, then switched abruptly to "bars" in immediately following definite לַבְּרִיחִם / הַבְּרִיחִם (36:34) and inventory summary בְּרִיחָו (39:33).
applied_changes: Harmonized "bars" -> "crossbars" in Exod 36:34 (2x; native_verses[36:34] & verses[38:18]) and Exod 39:33 (native_verses[39:33] & verses[39:13]), achieving 100% consistency across all 11 tabernacle בְּרִיחַ verses.
